extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and beginning graduate students studying algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Constructions and criteria for producing CW approximations, n-connected CW models, Postnikov towers, and related theorems (excision for homotopy, Freudenthal suspension, relations between weak homotopy equivalence and (co)homology/mapping-classes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitehead's theorem (CW version)
rubrics_metrics.description: A weak homotopy equivalence between CW complexes is a homotopy equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as the criterion that for CW complexes, isomorphisms on all homotopy groups (weak equivalence) suffice to conclude an honest homotopy equivalence. Immediately implies the same for spaces homotopy equivalent to CW complexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of CW approximations
rubrics_metrics.description: For every space X there is a CW complex Z and a weak homotopy equivalence f : Z → X. Such a map f : Z → X is called a CW approximation to X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct Z inductively by attaching cells to achieve the desired effect on homotopy groups stage by stage (see the inductive construction below). This lets one reduce many statements about arbitrary spaces to CW complexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of CW approximations up to homotopy
rubrics_metrics.description: CW approximations to a given space X are unique up to homotopy equivalence: if f : Z → X and f' : Z' → X are two CW approximations, then Z and Z' are homotopy equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose Z → X → Mf' and use the compression lemma to deform into Z' producing a weak homotopy equivalence Z → Z', hence a homotopy equivalence by Whitehead's theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inductive goal for attaching k-cells (condition (*))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a CW complex A with map f : A → X and chosen basepoint 0-cell in each component, attach k-cells to form B with f : B → X extending f such that: for each basepoint a_γ the induced map f_* : π_i(B, a_γ) → π_i(X, f(a_γ)) is injective for i = k−1 (when k > 0) and surjective for i = k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the local inductive target: at stage k one kills kernels in dimension k−1 and surjects onto π_k(X). Achieving (*) at each stage yields a CW approximation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step (1) of cell-attachment (k > 0): kill kernel elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose cellular maps ϕ_α : (S^{k−1}, s0) → (A, a_γ) representing all nontrivial elements of the kernels of f_* : π_{k−1}(A, a_γ) → π_{k−1}(X, f(a_γ)), and attach k-cells e^k_α along these maps, extending f over these cells by nullhomotopies of f∘ϕ_α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attaching these k-cells eliminates elements of the kernel on π_{k−1} so that injectivity in dimension k−1 is achieved. Use cellular maps for compatibility; nullhomotopies exist by choice of the ϕ_α.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step (2) of cell-attachment: realize π_k(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose maps f_β : S^k → X representing all nontrivial elements of π_k(X, f(a_γ)) (for the relevant basepoints) and attach k-cells e^k_β to A via the constant maps at the appropriate basepoints a_γ, extending f over the resulting spheres S^k via the maps f_β.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attaching these k-cells ensures surjectivity onto π_k(X); pick representatives (or generators) and attach one cell per representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency/generators note for attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: It suffices to attach cells just for generators of the kernels when k > 1, and just for generators of π_k(X, f(a_γ)) in step (2) when k > 0. Attaching k-cells does not affect π_i for i < k−1, and does not destroy surjectivity on π_{k−1} or any π_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize attachments by choosing generators; cellular approximation guarantees low-dimensional homotopy groups are unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staged construction starting from components
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with A consisting of one point for each path-component of X and map those points into X; attach 1-cells to create surjection on π_1 for each component, then 2-cells to improve to isomorphism on π_1 and surjection on π_2, and so on, producing Z with f : Z → X a weak homotopy equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed inductively through dimensions, achieving the injectivity/surjectivity targets at each stage to build the CW approximation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CW approximation for pairs and relative isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a pair (X, X_0) one can first construct a CW approximation f_0 : Z_0 → X_0 and then attach cells to Z_0 to create a weak homotopy equivalence f : Z → X extending f_0; by the five-lemma f : (Z, Z_0) → (X, X_0) induces isomorphisms on relative as well as absolute homotopy groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the relative mapping cylinder composition and the inductive cell-attachment technique to extend approximations from subspaces to pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: n-connected CW model (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An n-connected CW model for a pair (X, A) (with A a nonempty CW complex) is an n-connected CW pair (Z, A) and a map f : Z → X with f|_A the identity, such that f_* : π_i(Z) → π_i(X) is an isomorphism for i > n and an injection for i = n, for all choices of basepoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of Z as a homotopy-theoretic hybrid of A and X: π_i(A)→π_i(Z) is iso for i<n and surjective for i=n; in dimension n the factorization π_n(A)→π_n(Z)→π_n(X) is surjection followed by injection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of n-connected CW models (Proposition 4.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every pair (X, A) with A a nonempty CW complex there exist n-connected CW models f : (Z, A) → (X, A) for all n ≥ 0, and these models can be chosen so that Z is obtained from A by attaching cells of dimension greater than n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cell-attachment construction ensuring all new cells have dimension > n to obtain the required connectivity and mapping properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refinement to make cells > n (Proposition 4.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (X, A) is an n-connected CW pair, then there exists a CW pair (Z, A) ≃ (X, A) rel A such that all cells of Z − A have dimension greater than n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach cells of dimension n+1 and higher to A to produce Z with f : Z → X identity on A, injective on π_n and isomorphisms on higher groups; then use mapping-cylinder/quotient arguments to get homotopy equivalence rel A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality and uniqueness of n-connected models (Proposition 4.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given n-connected model f:(Z,A)→(X,A), n'-connected model f':(Z',A')→(X',A'), and map g:(X,A)→(X',A'), if n ≥ n' there exists h:Z→Z' with h|_A = g and g f ≃ f' h rel A; such h is unique up to homotopy rel A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compression lemma and relative mapping cylinders; this gives functorial maps between models and uniqueness up to homotopy rel A. Apply with g = id to get uniqueness of models up to homotopy rel A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitehead tower / n-connected covers (Example 4.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a CW complex X with A a point, there is a tower ... → Z_2 → Z_1 → Z_0 → X with Z_n n-connected and the map Z_n → X inducing isomorphism on π_i for i > n; Z_1 is simply-connected (universal cover analog), Z_n → X can be viewed as an 'n-connected cover'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct Zn as n-connected CW models; the tower maps are compatible and give successive approximations to X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak homotopy equivalence implies (co)homology isomorphism (Proposition 4.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: A weak homotopy equivalence f : X → Y induces isomorphisms f_* : H_n(X; G) → H_n(Y; G) and f^* : H^n(Y; G) → H^n(X; G) for all n and all coefficient groups G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to showing that if (Z, X) is n-connected and path-connected then H_i(Z, X; G) = 0 and H^i(Z, X; G) = 0 for all i ≤ n; use finite simplicial complexes built from singular chains, compression lemma, and universal coefficient theorem for cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak homotopy equivalence induces bijection on mapping classes (Proposition 4.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: A weak homotopy equivalence f : Y → Z induces bijections [X, Y] → [X, Z] and ⟨X, Y⟩ → ⟨X, Z⟩ for all CW complexes X (unpointed and pointed homotopy classes respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace f by inclusion via the mapping cylinder, then use vanishing of π_n(Z, Y) and the compression lemma to homotope any map X→Z into Y, giving surjectivity; relative version gives injectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision for homotopy groups (Theorem 4.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X = A ∪ B with nonempty connected intersection C = A ∩ B. If (A, C) is m-connected and (B, C) is n-connected, m, n ≥ 0, then inclusion induces an isomorphism π_i(A, C) → π_i(X, B) for i < m + n and a surjection for i = m + n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by detailed cell-pushing and dimension-counting arguments (Cases 1–3), using simplicial approximation (Lemma 4.10), compression lemma, and five-lemma inductively on cell dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freudenthal suspension theorem (Corollary 4.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspension map π_i(S^n) → π_{i+1}(S^{n+1}) is an isomorphism for i < 2n − 1 and a surjection for i = 2n − 1; more generally this holds for π_i(X) → π_{i+1}(SX) whenever X is an (n − 1)-connected CW complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the excision theorem to the decomposition of the suspension into two cones intersecting in X; convert to statement about relative groups and use connectivity estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of π_n(S^n) (Corollary 4.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: π_n(S^n) ≈ Z, generated by the identity map; the degree map π_n(S^n) → Z is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Freudenthal suspension result to relate π_n(S^n) to π_1(S^1) which is Z, and argue degree is preserved under suspension. Alternatively, use Hopf fibration to relate π_2(S^2) to π_1(S^1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient map on relative homotopy to quotient space (Proposition 4.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CW pair (X, A) is r-connected and A is s-connected (r, s ≥ 0), then the map π_i(X, A) → π_i(X/A) induced by the quotient map X → X/A is an isomorphism for i ≤ r + s and a surjection for i = r + s + 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a cone CA to A and identify X ∪ CA → X/A is a homotopy equivalence; apply excision to (CA, A) which is (s+1)-connected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on π_n when attaching (n+1)-cells to a wedge of spheres (Example 4.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is obtained from a wedge W of S^n's (n ≥ 2) by attaching (n+1)-cells via maps ϕ_β : S^n → W, then π_n(X) is the quotient of the free abelian group π_n(W) by the subgroup generated by the classes [ϕ_β]. Every abelian group can be realized in this way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the long exact sequence of the pair (X, W) and Proposition 4.26 about π_n of a wedge of spheres to identify the boundary map from π_{n+1}(X, W) (free abelian on attached cells) to π_n(W) with the attaching maps [ϕ_β].

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces K(G,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: One can build a CW complex K(G, n) for arbitrary G (abelian if n > 1) by starting with an (n−1)-connected CW complex of dimension n+1 with π_n ≈ G (as in Example 4.29), then attaching higher-dimensional cells to make π_i trivial for i > n without affecting π_n or lower groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the earlier cell-attachment technique iteratively to kill unwanted higher homotopy groups; for G abelian when n>1 ensure commutativity constraints are met.
